title: IL SB1507: VEH CD-SAFETY ZONES

obligations: A municipality that produces a recorded image of a motor vehicle's violation must make the recorded images accessible to the alleged violator by providing a website address accessible through the Internet (Sec. 11-208.8(b))

The automated speed enforcement system shall be operational and violations recorded only at specified times: for school district property, only on school days and no earlier than 6 a.m. and no later than 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday, or 9 p.m. on Friday; for park district property, no earlier than one hour before opening and no later than one hour after closing (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))

For each violation, the municipality having jurisdiction shall issue a written notice to the registered owner as the alleged violator, delivered by mail within 30 days after the Secretary of State notifies the municipality of the owner's identity, but no later than 90 days after the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(e))

The notice must include the owner's name and address, vehicle registration number, violation charged, date time and location, a copy of the recorded image or images, the civil penalty amount and payment date, a statement that recorded images are evidence, a warning that failure to pay or contest is an admission of liability, a statement of options to pay or challenge, and a website address to view images (Sec. 11-208.8(f))

A roadway equipped with an automated speed enforcement system shall be posted with a sign conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices visible to approaching traffic stating that vehicle speeds are being photo enforced and indicating the speed limit; the municipality shall install additional signage as it determines necessary (Sec. 11-208.8(l))

A roadway where a new automated speed enforcement system is installed shall be posted with signs providing 30 days notice of the use of a new system prior to issuance of any citations (Sec. 11-208.8(m))

The compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system must be based on the value of the equipment or services provided and may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or revenue generated (Sec. 11-208.8(n))

A municipality using an automated speed enforcement system must provide notice to drivers by publishing the locations of all safety zones where system equipment is installed on the municipality's website (Sec. 11-208.8(q))

A municipality operating an automated speed enforcement system shall conduct a statistical analysis to assess safety impact following installation and every 2 years thereafter; if operating before the effective date of the 103rd General Assembly amendatory Act, by no later than one year after that effective date and every 2 years thereafter; each analysis shall be based on best available crash, traffic, and other data, cover before and after periods, be consistent with professional judgment and industry practice, and be published on the municipality's website (Sec. 11-208.8(r))

The net proceeds from civil penalties, after deducting nonpersonnel and personnel costs, shall be expended or obligated for public safety initiatives around schools and parks, initiatives to improve pedestrian and traffic safety, construction and maintenance of infrastructure including roads and bridges, and after school programs (Sec. 11-208.8(d))

If a county or municipality selects a new vendor and must apply for a permit, approval, or other authorization from the Department for reinstallation of malfunctioning components, and the new vendor operates a system for any other county or municipality in the State, the Department shall approve or deny the application within 90 days after receipt (Sec. 11-208.8(t))

The Department shall adopt rules necessary to implement and administer the revocation process under subsection (u), including describing the revocation process, ensuring notice, and providing an opportunity to appeal (Sec. 11-208.8(u))

The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center shall conduct a study including review of City of Chicago website multi-year crash data on North and South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, available research on potential effectiveness of cameras powered by artificial intelligence in improving compliance and reducing crashes and road fatalities, analysis of driving behavior to detect risky driving patterns and address crash corridors, assessment of psychological deterrence in reducing habitual speeding, and assessment of how fatalities can be reduced using these cameras powered by artificial intelligence and other technical options (Sec. 11-208.8(v))

A lessor of a motor vehicle under a written lease agreement, upon request of the appropriate authority received within 120 days after the violation, shall provide within 60 days the name and address of the lessee (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
prohibitions: A penalty may not be imposed if the recorded speed of a vehicle is 5 miles per hour or less over the legal speed limit (Sec. 11-208.8(c))

A penalty may not be imposed if the driver received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the violation recorded by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(c))

A violation for which a civil penalty is imposed is not a violation of a traffic regulation governing the movement of vehicles and may not be recorded on the driving record of the owner (Sec. 11-208.8(c))

Recorded images made by an automated speed enforcement system are confidential and shall be made available only to the alleged violator and governmental and law enforcement agencies for purposes of adjudicating a violation, for statistical purposes, or for other governmental purposes (Sec. 11-208.8(i))

No member of the General Assembly and no officer or employee of a municipality or county shall knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees for services from a vendor that provides automated speed enforcement system equipment or services to municipalities or counties (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
No former member of the General Assembly shall, within 2 years after termination of service, knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees from such a vendor (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))

No former officer or employee of a municipality or county shall, within 2 years after termination of employment, knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees from such a vendor (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
The compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(n))

No person who is the lessor of a motor vehicle pursuant to a written lease agreement shall be liable for an automated speed or traffic law enforcement system violation involving such motor vehicle during the period of the lease, provided the lessor provides the lessee information as required (Sec. 11-208.8(p))

What it does

This Illinois law authorizes municipalities with at least 1,000,000 inhabitants to use automated speed enforcement systems in safety zones near schools and parks. It sets operating hours, notice requirements, civil penalties for speeding violations, and rules for use of revenue. It also requires a study of artificial intelligence powered cameras on Lake Shore Drive.

Who it applies to

  • Municipalities with a population of 1,000,000 or more inhabitants (Sec. 11-208.8(s))
  • Registered owners of motor vehicles recorded speeding in a safety zone (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • Lessors of motor vehicles under written lease agreements (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
  • Vendors providing automated speed enforcement system equipment or services (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
  • The Illinois Department of Transportation (Sec. 11-208.8(t), (u))
  • The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center (Sec. 11-208.8(v))

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Automated speed enforcement system: a photographic device, radar device, laser device, or other electrical or mechanical device or devices installed or utilized in a safety zone and designed to record the speed of a vehicle and obtain a clear photograph or other recorded image of the vehicle and the vehicle's registration plate or digital registration plate while the driver is violating Article VI of Chapter 11 of this Code or a similar provision of a local ordinance (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Owner: the person or entity to whom the vehicle is registered (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Recorded image: images recorded by an automated speed enforcement system on 2 or more photographs, 2 or more microphotographs, 2 or more electronic images, or a video recording showing the motor vehicle and, on at least one image or portion of the recording, clearly identifying the registration plate or digital registration plate number of the motor vehicle (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Safety zone: an area that is within one eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any public or private elementary or secondary school, or from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a school district that is used for educational purposes approved by the Illinois State Board of Education, not including school district headquarters or administrative buildings; also includes an area within one eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a park district used for recreational purposes; if any portion of a roadway is within either one eighth mile radius, the safety zone also includes the roadway extended to the furthest portion of the next furthest intersection; does not include any portion of Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Obligations

  • A municipality that produces a recorded image of a motor vehicle's violation must make the recorded images accessible to the alleged violator by providing a website address accessible through the Internet (Sec. 11-208.8(b))
  • The automated speed enforcement system shall be operational and violations recorded only at specified times: for school district property, only on school days and no earlier than 6 a.m. and no later than 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday, or 9 p.m. on Friday; for park district property, no earlier than one hour before opening and no later than one hour after closing (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))
  • For each violation, the municipality having jurisdiction shall issue a written notice to the registered owner as the alleged violator, delivered by mail within 30 days after the Secretary of State notifies the municipality of the owner's identity, but no later than 90 days after the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(e))
  • The notice must include the owner's name and address, vehicle registration number, violation charged, date time and location, a copy of the recorded image or images, the civil penalty amount and payment date, a statement that recorded images are evidence, a warning that failure to pay or contest is an admission of liability, a statement of options to pay or challenge, and a website address to view images (Sec. 11-208.8(f))
  • A roadway equipped with an automated speed enforcement system shall be posted with a sign conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices visible to approaching traffic stating that vehicle speeds are being photo enforced and indicating the speed limit; the municipality shall install additional signage as it determines necessary (Sec. 11-208.8(l))
  • A roadway where a new automated speed enforcement system is installed shall be posted with signs providing 30 days notice of the use of a new system prior to issuance of any citations (Sec. 11-208.8(m))
  • The compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system must be based on the value of the equipment or services provided and may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or revenue generated (Sec. 11-208.8(n))
  • A municipality using an automated speed enforcement system must provide notice to drivers by publishing the locations of all safety zones where system equipment is installed on the municipality's website (Sec. 11-208.8(q))
  • A municipality operating an automated speed enforcement system shall conduct a statistical analysis to assess safety impact following installation and every 2 years thereafter; if operating before the effective date of the 103rd General Assembly amendatory Act, by no later than one year after that effective date and every 2 years thereafter; each analysis shall be based on best available crash, traffic, and other data, cover before and after periods, be consistent with professional judgment and industry practice, and be published on the municipality's website (Sec. 11-208.8(r))
  • The net proceeds from civil penalties, after deducting nonpersonnel and personnel costs, shall be expended or obligated for public safety initiatives around schools and parks, initiatives to improve pedestrian and traffic safety, construction and maintenance of infrastructure including roads and bridges, and after school programs (Sec. 11-208.8(d))
  • If a county or municipality selects a new vendor and must apply for a permit, approval, or other authorization from the Department for reinstallation of malfunctioning components, and the new vendor operates a system for any other county or municipality in the State, the Department shall approve or deny the application within 90 days after receipt (Sec. 11-208.8(t))
  • The Department shall adopt rules necessary to implement and administer the revocation process under subsection (u), including describing the revocation process, ensuring notice, and providing an opportunity to appeal (Sec. 11-208.8(u))
  • The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center shall conduct a study including review of City of Chicago website multi-year crash data on North and South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, available research on potential effectiveness of cameras powered by artificial intelligence in improving compliance and reducing crashes and road fatalities, analysis of driving behavior to detect risky driving patterns and address crash corridors, assessment of psychological deterrence in reducing habitual speeding, and assessment of how fatalities can be reduced using these cameras powered by artificial intelligence and other technical options (Sec. 11-208.8(v))
  • A lessor of a motor vehicle under a written lease agreement, upon request of the appropriate authority received within 120 days after the violation, shall provide within 60 days the name and address of the lessee (Sec. 11-208.8(p))

Prohibitions

  • A penalty may not be imposed if the recorded speed of a vehicle is 5 miles per hour or less over the legal speed limit (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • A penalty may not be imposed if the driver received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the violation recorded by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • A violation for which a civil penalty is imposed is not a violation of a traffic regulation governing the movement of vehicles and may not be recorded on the driving record of the owner (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • Recorded images made by an automated speed enforcement system are confidential and shall be made available only to the alleged violator and governmental and law enforcement agencies for purposes of adjudicating a violation, for statistical purposes, or for other governmental purposes (Sec. 11-208.8(i))
  • No member of the General Assembly and no officer or employee of a municipality or county shall knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees for services from a vendor that provides automated speed enforcement system equipment or services to municipalities or counties (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
  • No former member of the General Assembly shall, within 2 years after termination of service, knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees from such a vendor (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
  • No former officer or employee of a municipality or county shall, within 2 years after termination of employment, knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees from such a vendor (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
  • The compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(n))
  • No person who is the lessor of a motor vehicle pursuant to a written lease agreement shall be liable for an automated speed or traffic law enforcement system violation involving such motor vehicle during the period of the lease, provided the lessor provides the lessee information as required (Sec. 11-208.8(p))

Penalties and enforcement

The municipality having jurisdiction issues the written notice of violation and imposes civil penalties. Penalties are: if recorded speed is 6 to 10 miles per hour over the legal limit, a civil penalty not exceeding $50, plus an additional penalty of not more than $50 for failure to pay timely; if recorded speed is more than 10 miles per hour over, a civil penalty not exceeding $100, plus an additional penalty of not more than $100 for failure to pay timely (Sec. 11-208.8(c)). A law enforcement officer is not required to be present or witness the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(c)). The court or hearing officer may consider defenses including stolen vehicle or plates, hijacking, receipt of a Uniform Traffic Citation, and any other evidence or issues provided by municipal ordinance (Sec. 11-208.8(j)). To demonstrate theft or hijacking, the owner or lessee must submit proof that a report was filed with a law enforcement agency in a timely manner (Sec. 11-208.8(k)). The Department may revoke any permit, approval, or other authorization granted to a county or municipality for placement, installation, or operation of an automated speed enforcement system if any official or employee who serves that county or municipality is charged with bribery, official misconduct, or a similar crime related to the system (Sec. 11-208.8(u)). A county or municipality with a revoked permit may not reapply for 1 year (Sec. 11-208.8(u)). No private right of action is stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • The law does not directly regulate artificial intelligence systems; it regulates automated speed enforcement systems, which are defined as photographic, radar, laser, or other electrical or mechanical devices, without explicit mention of AI (Sec. 11-208.8(a)).
  • Subsection (v) requires the University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center to study the potential effectiveness of cameras powered by artificial intelligence in improving compliance and reducing crashes and road fatalities on North and South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, and to assess how fatalities can be reduced using these cameras and other technical options (Sec. 11-208.8(v)).
  • An organisation deploying an automated speed enforcement system that uses AI would need to comply with all operational, notice, signage, data confidentiality, revenue use, and statistical analysis requirements of this Section, because the definition of automated speed enforcement system is broad enough to include electrical or mechanical devices (Sec. 11-208.8(a), (b), (d), (e), (f), (i), (l), (m), (n), (q), (r)).

Notable exemptions

  • The term safety zone does not include any portion of the roadway known as Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic (Sec. 11-208.8(a)).
  • No penalty may be imposed if the recorded speed is 5 miles per hour or less over the legal speed limit (Sec. 11-208.8(c)).
  • No penalty may be imposed if the driver received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the violation recorded by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(c)).
  • A lessor under a written lease agreement is not liable for a violation during the lease period if the lessor provides the lessee's name and address within 60 days of a request received within 120 days after the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(p)).
  • This Section applies only to municipalities with a population of 1,000,000 or more inhabitants (Sec. 11-208.8(s)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the municipality has a population of 1,000,000 or more inhabitants, because the Section applies only to such municipalities (Sec. 11-208.8(s)).
  • Identify safety zones within one eighth of a mile from school or park district property, excluding Lake Shore Drive and controlled access highways with 8 or more lanes (Sec. 11-208.8(a)).
  • Ensure the automated speed enforcement system is operational only during the permitted hours for school or park safety zones (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5)).
  • Post signs conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices indicating photo enforcement and speed limit, and install additional signage as necessary (Sec. 11-208.8(l)).
  • For any new automated speed enforcement system, post signs providing 30 days notice before issuing citations (Sec. 11-208.8(m)).
  • Ensure vendor compensation is based on equipment or services value, not on citations or revenue (Sec. 11-208.8(n)).
  • Comply with employment restrictions for General Assembly members, municipal and county officers and employees, and former officials regarding vendors (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1)).
  • Issue written notices of violation to registered owners by mail within 30 days after Secretary of State notification and no later than 90 days after violation, including all required content (Sec. 11-208.8(e), (f)).
  • Make recorded images accessible to the alleged violator through a website address (Sec. 11-208.8(b)).
  • Keep recorded images confidential and disclose only to the alleged violator and governmental and law enforcement agencies for permitted purposes (Sec. 11-208.8(i)).
  • Use net proceeds from civil penalties only for the specified purposes: public safety initiatives around schools and parks, pedestrian and traffic safety improvements, infrastructure construction and maintenance, and after school programs (Sec. 11-208.8(d)).
  • Publish the locations of all safety zones where system equipment is installed on the municipality's website (Sec. 11-208.8(q)).
  • Conduct and publish a statistical analysis of safety impact after installation and every 2 years thereafter, or within one year if operating before the effective date of the 103rd General Assembly amendatory Act (Sec. 11-208.8(r)).
  • If selecting a new vendor requiring Department approval, ensure the Department approves or denies within 90 days if the vendor operates elsewhere in the State (Sec. 11-208.8(t)).
  • Be aware that the Department may revoke permits if an official or employee is charged with bribery, official misconduct, or similar crime related to the system, and that reapplication is barred for 1 year after revocation (Sec. 11-208.8(u)).
  • If a lessor is involved, upon request received within 120 days after violation, obtain lessee information within 60 days and issue the violation to the lessee (Sec. 11-208.8(p)).
